questions.question: What does a reducer function receive and return?
options: Props and children, returning JSX
The current state and an action, returning the next state
An action and a dispatch, returning nothing
The previous props, returning a boolean
questions.explanation: `(state, action) => nextState` is the whole contract. Keeping it pure is what makes it predictable and testable.

questions.question: Which situation most clearly calls for useReducer over useState?
options: A single boolean toggle
Several state values that always change together in the same handlers
A value read from a prop
A ref to a DOM node
questions.explanation: When transitions touch several values at once, a reducer collects them into one place instead of scattering them across handlers.

questions.question: Why is this reducer case wrong?
options: push is not allowed in JavaScript
It mutates the existing state instead of returning a new object
The action type should be a string constant
It should return undefined
questions.explanation: Mutating state keeps the same references, so React may skip the re-render, and it breaks the purity a reducer depends on. Return new objects and arrays.

questions.question: Why should crypto.randomUUID() be called in the component rather than in the reducer?
options: It is slower inside a reducer
It makes the reducer impure, producing different results for the same inputs
Reducers cannot access browser APIs
It would generate invalid ids
questions.explanation: A pure reducer must return the same state for the same inputs. Generate the id where the event happens and pass it in the action.

questions.question: How should actions be named?
options: After the field they set, such as setLoading
After what happened, such as submitted or deleted
After the component that dispatched them
With numeric codes
questions.explanation: Event-style names let the reducer own the consequences, so a single action can update several values without the component knowing the internals.

questions.question: What is true of the dispatch function returned by useReducer?
options: It changes identity on every render
It is stable for the life of the component, so it is safe to omit from dependency arrays
It must be memoised with useCallback
It re-creates the reducer
questions.explanation: React guarantees a stable `dispatch`, which is why passing it through context does not cause consumer re-renders.

questions.question: What problem do TanStack Query and SWR solve that a reducer does not?
options: Rendering lists efficiently
Caching, refetching and deduplicating server data along with its loading and error states
Type checking state
Styling components
questions.explanation: They handle server state - a cache of remote data - which is where most hand-written loading and error reducer code comes from.

questions.question: Write the toggle case of a todo reducer
questions.explanation: Immutable updates with map keep the other items untouched while replacing the one that changed.

editor.title: Toggle a todo
editor.instructions: Complete toggleTodo so it returns a new array where the item with the given id has its done value flipped.

tests.name: Flipping twice restores it
tests.code: var once = toggleTodo([{id:1,done:false}], 1); return toggleTodo(once, 1)[0].done === false;

tests.name: The original array is not mutated
tests.code: var list = [{id:1,done:false}]; toggleTodo(list, 1); return list[0].done === false;
